html:
Saparmurat Niyazov ruled Turkmenistan from 1985, as Soviet party chief, until his death in 2006, calling himself Turkmenbashi, head of all Turkmen. He was born in 1940 near Ashgabat and lost most of his family in the earthquake of 1948.

After independence he was named president for life. He built a cult unlike any since Stalin: a gold statue that turned with the sun, months renamed after himself and his mother, and his book, the Ruhnama, made compulsory reading in schools and for driving tests. He closed hospitals outside the capital and cut schooling.

Gas exports paid for marble buildings in Ashgabat and free gas, water and salt for citizens. Rivals were jailed and the country was shut to the world. His successor, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, dropped some of his excesses but kept the system.
